title: Reverse De La Riva Guard
description: RDLR uses an outside thigh hook and hip rotation to create angle, sweep, or transition to other guards.
topPlayerGoals: The top player wants to control Reverse De La Riva Guard through Head Position, Inside Position, and directed pressure.
Kill the hook, staple the leg, and drive shoulder line down.
Keep a stable base so you are not off-balanced or countered.
bottomPlayerGoals: The bottom player wants to survive Reverse De La Riva Guard with frames, Pummeling, or the right angle.
Keep the hook alive, turn hips outward, and choose sweep, Kimura, or back take.
Recognize danger signals early instead of waiting for the position to settle.
controlPoints: Main control point: Outside hook, hip angle, and far wrist.
Head, hands, hips, and knees should share the same force direction.
The Elbow-Knee Connection or hip-shoulder line determines whether the position is still alive or already locked.
escapePriorities: Escape priority: Do not let them pull the far wrist across the hip line.
Protect the neck, back, Knee Line, or arm line before countering.
If Inside Position is lost, reset one defensive layer first.

advancementOptions.action: Transition to DLR or enter Berimbolo lines
advancementOptions.why: This is the natural branch when you win the main control point and the opponent is forced to defend.

dangerSignals: The chin or neck is pulled out of a safe line.
The elbow separates from the ribs or knee.
The hip line is locked while the shoulder line is still being pulled.
You need a long hand post to avoid falling.
